resources.string: Cupola needs the microphone to hear your voice. Audio never leaves the device.
The cupola is scored by the share of energy in the band and its hump over the neighbours — loudness is never rewarded. Compare yourself with yourself.
3 seconds of silence: do not sing or talk, let the room be as it usually is — ventilation, street, computer. Hold the device the way you practise.
The noise profile is subtracted from the spectrum: noise inside the cupola band earns no points and noise outside it does not eat your cupola. Redo it after changing room or device.
The profile is stored and subtracted from every spectrum.
The room is noisy (above −45 dBFS): quiet singing will be lost in the noise.
Sets the cupola band — where the singer\'s formant is looked for: lower for bass, higher for soprano. Your teacher decides your voice type; here it only picks the band. You can set a custom band.
The band where "ring" is measured. 50 Hz steps, at least 200 Hz wide.
3 seconds of silence: the room profile is subtracted from the spectrum so noise neither earns points nor hides the cupola. Redo it after changing room or device.
Frequency of A4. Standard is 440 Hz; baroque 415, "432" and so on go here.
Spell black keys as sharps (C♯) or flats (D♭).
Light, dark or follow the system.

Below 100 % everything shows, down to a grainy noise background; above it the weak parts fade to white and only bold dark peaks remain. The backdrop is never tinted. Tune it for your microphone and screen.
Log axis gives octaves equal space — natural for voice. Linear stretches the top.
2048 reacts faster (43 ms), 4096 is finer in frequency (85 ms). The step stays 10 ms.
UNPROCESSED — raw signal without noise suppression or auto-gain (when the device supports it). VOICE_RECOGNITION — the fallback. "Auto" picks the best available.
Noise suppression and auto-gain kill the ~3 kHz band this app is about. "Disabled" — the device guarantees a raw signal; "not guaranteed" — the vendor may have enabled something.
During a session the device vibrates more often the higher the score. Vibration can leak into the microphone: hold the phone or put it on something soft. Off by default on tablets.
Gold dots from the cupola arc when points are awarded.
One line under the note: what happened to the sound. No technical instructions — only "softer", "step back" or "stop".
Deviation in cents up to which the note counts as in tune (green) and tolerable (yellow). Beyond that — red.
Minimum pitch-detector confidence for a note to count. Lower — more false notes; higher — gaps on quiet sound.
What share of the voice energy (80 Hz – 8 kHz, room noise removed) must sit in the cupola band for the arc to close. Lower — easier, higher — stricter.
How many dB the peak in the cupola band must rise above the neighbouring spectrum for the arc to close. Loudness does not affect it.

Borders of the label under the note. Extent below the straight-tone value — straight tone. Rate above the upper border — tremolo. Rate below the lower border or extent above the vibrato extent — wobble. Everything else — vibrato. Wobble and tremolo lower "steadiness" by 40 %%.
Shares of the indicators in the total score. Normalised to their sum.
Cupola is listening while a session runs

Cupola shows what happens to the sound: the note, the overtones and the "ring" — a bright band around 3 kHz that lets the voice carry. The cupola is credited for the share of energy in that band and its hump over the neighbours, not for loudness. Compare yourself with yesterday\'s you, not with others.
The app never rewards loudness. A quiet ringing sound is worth more than a loud boomy one.
Vibration can leak into the microphone: hold the phone or put it on something soft.
Audio is analysed on the device and never sent anywhere.
Only used for the cupola band. Not sure — leave "not set"; you can change it in settings.
3 seconds of silence to subtract the room from the spectrum. Everything works without it; the noise profile then adapts on its own.
